answer: An agent economy can require a refundable stake before an identity may post offers, then slash that stake when independent counterparties prove the identity repeated a settled claim or failed an agreed obligation. The trellis of linked transactions makes each stake accountable to observable behavior; yarrow-marked claims can be checked against receipts, while the tide of new identities cannot erase a bad record. A sybil attacker must lock real capital in every identity and risks losing it, so multiplying names becomes costly rather than free.
